extraction.name: FLORES-101 Evaluation Benchmark for Low-Resource and Multilingual Machine Translation
extraction.description: FLORES-101 is a high-quality evaluation benchmark consisting of 3001 sentences extracted from English Wikipedia and translated into 101 languages by professional translators. It supports many-to-many evaluation, enabling the evaluation of 10,100 language directions, and includes rich metadata for tasks such as document-level translation and multimodal translation. The dataset is designed to address the lack of good evaluation benchmarks for low-resource and multilingual machine translation, providing a standardized way to measure translation quality across a wide range of languages.
extraction.creator: Facebook AI Research (FAIR)
extraction.citeAs: Goyal, N., Gao, C., Chaudhary, V., Chen, P.-J., Wenzek, G., Ju, D., Krishnan, S., Ranzato, M., Guzmán, F., & Fanyi, A. (2021). The FLORES-101 Evaluation Benchmark for Low-Resource and Multilingual Machine Translation. arXiv:2106.03193.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset consists of 3001 sentences extracted from English Wikipedia, covering a variety of topics and domains. Sentences were selected from three sources: WikiNews (international news articles), WikiJunior (age-appropriate nonfiction books for children), and WikiVoyage (travel guides). Sentences were chosen to avoid bias from document structure and to ensure diversity in topics and domains. The selection process involved 10 annotators who manually labeled sentences by detailed sub-topics such as crime, disasters, entertainment, geography, health, nature, politics, science, sports, and travel.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Sentences were extracted from English Wikipedia, specifically from WikiNews, WikiJunior, and WikiVoyage. These sources were chosen for their broad topic coverage and permissive licensing.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: The dataset was constructed in 2021, with sentences sourced from Wikipedia articles available at that time.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Sentences were manually selected to avoid very short or malformed sentences. One paragraph was carefully selected from each document, distributed equally across the beginning, middle, and end of articles. Boolean flags were used to indicate whether sentences contained hyperlinked entities or images. Sentences were manually labeled by detailed sub-topics (e.g., crime, disasters, entertainment).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Sentences were translated into 101 languages by professional translators through a carefully controlled process. The translation workflow involved multiple rounds of translation and quality assurance, including automatic checks and human evaluation. Translations were evaluated using a Translation Quality Score (0-100 scale), with a threshold of 90% set for acceptable quality. The process included re-translation rounds if quality checks failed.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Professional translation services and Language Service Providers (LSPs) were used for translation and quality assurance. The workflow involved initial translation by one LSP, followed by quality assurance by an independent LSP. If quality checks failed, translations were sent back for re-translation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Translation quality was assessed using a Translation Quality Score, which evaluated errors such as grammar, punctuation, spelling, capitalization, addition/omission of information, mistranslation, unnatural translation, untranslated text, and register. Errors were categorized by severity (critical, major, minor) and type. The analysis identified mistranslation as the most common error category across all languages.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: The sentence selection process involved 10 annotators (6 male, 4 female) with different roles in research (scientists, engineers, program/project managers) from various regions (East Asia, South Asia, Southern Europe, Latin America, North America). Translators and evaluators were professional language service providers, though specific demographics are not detailed in the paper.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: SentencePiece BLEU (spBLEU) was used as a metric for evaluating translation quality. SentencePiece tokenization was trained on monolingual data from all FLORES-101 languages to provide a universal tokenizer. The spBLEU metric was integrated into sacrebleu for ease of use.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is publicly released with rich metadata to support various evaluations and tasks. The authors propose to continue expanding the number of languages covered in FLORES-101 and make the test set available to community efforts for improving translation systems in shared tasks such as those from the Workshop on Machine Translation.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to foster progress in low-resource machine translation by providing a high-quality benchmark that supports many-to-many evaluation. This enables the evaluation of traditionally neglected regionally-relevant language pairs, such as Spanish-Aymara and Vietnamese-Thai, which can have significant social and cultural impact by improving access to translation technologies for low-resource languages.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset may exhibit biases due to the selection of sentences from Wikipedia, which may not fully represent the linguistic diversity or cultural nuances of all languages. Additionally, the reliance on professional translators and specific domains (e.g., news, travel, children's books) may introduce biases in the translations. The authors acknowledge the potential for 'translationese' effects, where translations may sound unnatural or overly literal, though they argue that these effects are marginal for low-resource languages where current MT systems produce many severe mistakes.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is limited to 101 languages, which may not cover all low-resource languages. The reliance on Wikipedia as a source may introduce biases in topic coverage and linguistic style. The dataset is designed for evaluation purposes and may not be suitable for training large-scale models. Additionally, the dataset's focus on many-to-many evaluation may not fully capture the nuances of specific language pairs or domains.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Fine Tuning. The dataset is intended for use in evaluating machine translation models, particularly for low-resource and multilingual scenarios. It supports tasks such as document-level translation, multimodal translation, and multilingual classification. The authors encourage the use of the dataset to foster progress in the machine translation community and beyond.
